diagnostic_evidence.quote: Furthermore, the order of convergence of the degree $2q+1$ method is $q+1$ \cite{doi:10.1137/0708036}.
Let $h \in \mathbb{P}_q$ be $[q/0]$ Padé-approximant to $(1-x)^{-1/2}$ \cite[Section 3]{kenney1991rational} and define $p(x) = xh(1-x^2) \in \mathbb{P}_d^{\odd}$.

issues.failure_explanation: For the degree d=2q+1 polynomial Padé (Newton–Schulz-type) iteration, the cited Kenney–Laub result gives 1 - x_{k}^2 ≤ (1-x_0^2)^{(q+1)^k}, i.e. order of convergence q+1 (as the paper itself states in the related-work section). The proof instead asserts the bound |1-x^2|^{(d+1)^T}/(1+f(x)) with d+1 = 2q+2, which is not what the invoked theorem yields and is false (e.g. for d=3 one step of Newton–Schulz gives 1-p(x)^2 = (1-x^2)^2(1-x^2/4), order 2 not 4). The derived bound therefore does not follow from the cited input; the theorem statement's exponent (q+1)^T is the correct one, so the written proof does not match the statement it proves.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace (d+1)^T by (q+1)^T in both lines of the proof, matching Kenney–Laub Theorem 3.1 for the [q/0] Padé iteration; the rest of the argument (optimality of p* over the Newton–Schulz composition, 1+f ≥ 1, monotonicity in x) then yields the stated bound.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of Theorem convergence as written is invalid (it derives a stronger, false intermediate bound); the statement itself, with exponent (q+1)^T and the quadratic/cubic claims for d=3,5, remains correct once the exponent in the proof is corrected.
issues.title: Proof of convergence theorem uses exponent (d+1)^T, inconsistent with the cited Padé result and with the stated (q+1)^T
issues.why_classification: A local correction of the exponent restores a valid proof of exactly the stated result; no claim, rate, or scope is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: There exists a unique polynomial $p^{\star} \in \mathbb{P}_d^{\odd}$ solving \eqref{eq:oneiteration}.
if and only if there exist $q+2$ distinct points $\{x_0,\ldots,x_{q+1}\} \subset [\ell,u]$
Intuitively, when $\ell = u$, the polynomial $p^*$ is coincides exactly with the Newton-Schulz method.

issues.failure_explanation: The lemma is stated for arbitrary u, ℓ > 0 without requiring ℓ < u. If ℓ = u the domain [ℓ,u] is a single point, and every odd polynomial with p(u)=1 (e.g. p(x)=x/u and the Newton–Schulz polynomial scaled to u) attains error 0, so the minimizer is not unique and no q+2 distinct points exist in [ℓ,u]; Chebyshev's theorem requires the domain to contain at least q+2 points. Thus the existence-and-uniqueness and the 'if and only if' characterization fail in this case, and the prose assertion that p* 'coincides exactly with Newton-Schulz' when ℓ = u is unsupported (the argmin in eq. greedy is then ill-defined).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis 0 < ℓ < u to the lemma (and hence to Theorem greedy's inputs), or explicitly define p* in the case ℓ = u as the scaled Padé/Newton–Schulz polynomial; note that ℓ_t < u_t propagates automatically for t ≥ 2.
issues.overall_effect: Only the degenerate boundary case ℓ = u is affected; for 0 < ℓ < u (the case actually used, and later intervals automatically satisfy ℓ_{t+1} < u_{t+1} since the error is never zero) the lemma, Lemma computableerror, and Theorem greedy stand as proved.
issues.title: Equioscillation lemma claims a unique minimax polynomial for all u, ℓ > 0, false in the degenerate case ℓ = u
issues.why_classification: Adding a standard non-degeneracy hypothesis (ℓ < u) fixes the statement with no loss to any substantive result.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Hence, when $\ell/u \geq 1-\epsilon_d^{1/3}$, where $\epsilon_{\text{double}} \approx 1.1 \times 10^{-16}$ is the double precision machine epsilon, then $|p^{\star}(x) - p(x)| \leq 2 \epsilon_{\text{double}}$.

issues.failure_explanation: The Kenney–Laub bound for the degree-5 Padé polynomial gives 1 - p(x) ≤ (1-(x/u)^2)^3/(1+p(x)), so max over [ℓ,u] of |1-p| is bounded by (1-(ℓ/u)^2)^3 = (1-ℓ/u)^3(1+ℓ/u)^3, up to 8(1-ℓ/u)^3, not (1-ℓ/u)^3. The stated inequality 2·max|1-p| ≤ 2(1-ℓ/u)^3 is false; e.g. ℓ/u = 1/2 gives 1-p(1/2) ≈ 0.207 > (1/2)^3 = 0.125. Consequently the derived threshold guarantee |p*-p| ≤ 2ε_double for ℓ/u ≥ 1-ε_double^{1/3} is only |p*-p| ≤ 16ε_double.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the bound by 2(1-(ℓ/u)^2)^3 ≤ 16(1-ℓ/u)^3 and restate the conclusion as |p*-p| ≤ 16ε_double (or adjust the threshold to ℓ/u ≥ 1 - (ε_double/8)^{1/3}).
issues.overall_effect: The quantitative justification for the early-return branch in Algorithm remezdeg5 and the code threshold is off by a constant factor (up to 8); the qualitative conclusion that p* equals p to within a small multiple of machine epsilon survives.
issues.title: Claimed closeness bound 2(1-ℓ/u)^3 between optimal quintic and Padé polynomial drops the (1+ℓ/u)^3 factor
issues.why_classification: A constant-factor correction in an auxiliary numerical justification; the algorithm and all main results are unaffected.
